A little background:

  • A war is being raged and the group of 4 PC's have come together because they all have done various small favours to generals during the war. Because of this they are occasionally appointed to lead small advance guards and complete covert ops such as taking out the head of the enemy army.
  • My campaign is using the continent of Khorvaire's map, political boundaries, city locations/names and the Eberron setting (warforged and the like), but is not using any of the already established lore, political systems, monarchs, etc. Map of Khorvaire
  • One of my players is the stereotypical LN hermit human monk that desires balance and dislikes being around other people. Her "reason" for leaving seclusion is the war encroached on her metaphorical door step, and she discovered a great evil (gotta love the number of potential story hooks from her). Her back story was really kind of open ended as well...

Enter Gilgran's Core!

The Core of Gilgran the Great Dragon

To kind of facilitate the whole great evil thing, I made sure she was equipped with Gilgran the Great Dragon's core. The dragons are returning to further their agendas, thus the possessor of the core is charged with keeping balance. Gilgran is supposed to kind of serve as the mediary between metallic and chromatic dragons. A third dragon deity of balance that both sides generally hate. Gilgran itself is an it because it is a conglomerate of all the essences and spirits it has ever absorbed. Therefore the cost of using Gilgran's Core is that your spirit becomes bound to Gilgran's and upon death your spirit fuses with Gilgran's. That gives the item the massive downside of death becomes permanent regardless of anything else.

Any thoughts, comments, questions, opinions are appreciated and I'll be happy to respond to them!!!

TL;DR homebrew dragon deity artifact for boring monk

A couple questions and opinions:

  1. How does one come to obtain the core? The lore indicates that the appearance of the artifact is a sort of sign of dragon-stuff going on and a "champion" would wield it. Does it exists in the material plane? Is it protected by an ancient order of some sort and given to the chosen one? Does it manifest itself in time of need?

  2. How are charges for "Aversion to Death" regained? The text states that the user has a number of charges = (level / 2) + CON. Do these charges come back after a short/long rest?

  3. If the artifact truly requires the essence of other lifeforms to sustain itself then I think the damage to the user should be more gradual as the artifact begins to sap life from the user. So maybe after 7 days it begins doing 1d4 necrotic damage every few hours or so, then steps up to 1d8 the next day, 1d10 the next, etc, etc. This would make it happen more often i'd think because the user would otherwise stay up all night trying to drain something before completing a long rest after the 7th day, knowing that there a massive wave of hurt coming if they didn't. Whereas if it were gradual they may just take the damage if they are in a bind. Just a thought :)

  4. The end of "Dragon Absorption" says that obtaining 50 charges worth of essence opens up more of Gilgran's power to the user. What does this mean exactly and is there a chart showing the different tiers of power?

  5. Similar to the other features, is there a limit on the number of charges for "Spiritual Knowledge"?

Overall, I think combining the power source of the artifact for the various features might be easier and make more sense. So instead of each feature having its own rules and power, have a chart and system for storing and recovering "charges." Then each feature should expend a specified number of charges per use, all from the same pool. My first thought would be to have the "Dragon Absorption" feature tie into the number of charges the wielder has access to.

I also think that such a powerful artifact should be very difficult and draining to use at first, so even a single use of "Aversion to Death" at the beginning stages should almost completely deplete it.

Lots of questions!

  1. So the Core possesses the conscious of Gilgran. It isn't stated (but will be added) that Gilgran has some semblance of control over its core. The artifact is meant to eventually become sentient. For now though Gilgran is too weak to manifest a voice or anything. And yes the item is generally hidden in the material plane by Gilgran's magic or by the previous user upon death. So if my PC has reached the end of their life through old age then they are expected to hide it, put it in a temple for the next Champion to find, etc.

  2. That's something I totally missed. Long rest is what it is about to say XD

  3. I thought about making the damage lower, but the immediate massive damage after a long rest is supposed to heavily emphasise that they failed to drain. The necrotic damage if they fail to drain was just put in to show that the item HAS TO BE SATED in some way. They CAN feed it part of their own life force at the cost of disadvantage for 2 days (also recall the PC has a full week to make sure they've drained something). However, Gilgran desires the essences and souls of as many creatures as possible(that is how Gilgran's Draconic Greed is expressed).

  4. Yeah so Gilgran's Spirit lies dormant in the core when not maintained through the taking of souls and essences. The Core also does not care if the user is powerful and actually prefers those with untapped potential. Once the Core reaches 50 charges then the artifact will "level up". The power caps on properties will be reduced and it will generally become stronger. This will also unlock stronger Properties for the user to control. My player will be using this exact sheet and I totally didn't wanna ruin the surprise of how the Core will evolve. (oh and Gilgran will awaken, causing the item to become talkative to the PC)

  5. Nope! Spiritual knowledge is just supposed to show that Gilgran gains knowledge from every creature absorbed. That means that the PC could potentially have a massive number of charges. That would be kinda useless though as the charges only have a value if they're used.

There were a few reasons I had the artifact set up with different charge systems. I really needed the "Aversion to Death" part separate in charges as the PC CANNOT be revived in any way whatsoever!!! The "Dragon Absorption" was gonna have to be separate to keep track of exclusively dragon essences. And the "Spiritual Knowledge" is just meant to be the icing on the cake in a way.

The Core gives disadvantage on everything and half's movement for a month upon first binding to the user. Also as a side note: The Core was supposed to give almost no direct combat bonuses and that's why the drain is the only thing with a semi offensive use. (the target has disadvantage attacking you but you have disadvantage attacking the target)

Thanks for the feedback! I'm happy to discuss anything else you can think of for it.

My only suggestion would be related to the Essence Greed feature. It says that the core can only be used on creatures of a CR of 1 or higher. That's fine, it means you can't just carry around some goblins to feed it once a week, but as the party grows in level a CR 1 encounter would be easy enough for them to force it. "We find a bear in the woods and I use the core on it."

I would balance that by saying the target must be within a certain CR range of the attuned user. Possibly a plus or minus 2 CR range, that way encounters with more monsters could still provide a target, but a large battle against many weak monsters (though still a CR 1 or above) wouldn't "sate the greed" of the core.

If it works the way you like it though, just work with players when the need arises on anything you find too unbalanced.

100% agree. Once the item increases in power then it will require higher CR creatures for Essence Greed and gain other properties. I intentionally made the item with the idea that it will change and grow with the Character.

Dear Diary,

On advice from my doc during my physical, I saw a specialist about the bump on my head. Surgery is scheduled for next week, barring complications found in xrays. I don't know how I'm going to pay for all of this. The physical, I thought was free, but reading over the claim, it seems insurance only paid half. Near as I can estimate, that visit will set me back $300. The specialist plus surgery? I can't even begin to imagine. My individual deductible is in the thousands. I don't have thousands to spend. I don't have hundreds. What little I've saved for a car down payment will go towards health costs, I guess... plus more debt for a few months.

Haven't written anything for the novel in over a week. I get up the motivation to try and start, but something else calls me away. Work, sleep, a game, a walk. It's my own fault. No one to blame but me. I need to finish the ten or twenty thousand words or so that are left, but this lethargy is overwhelming. At least, I'm letting it be.

Someone I wanted to see was back in town this weekend and didn't visit... didn't even let me know. Reasons given make sense, I guess, but I can't help but feel lonely. I used to think that I loved this woman. A part of me still does. Most of me just cycles through a negativity loop of "she never has and never will love you." They say that people who do want to be in your life will make the time to do so, no matter what. I suppose I have my answer. The only thing left to do is get over it... and myself. It should be easy to let go, but it never is. I guess I fall too hard, too easily.

I hate these down phases. Everything seems bleak and worthless. The things that give me joy only seem to be holding me down. I want to write. I want to finish this novel and get it (and its predecessor) ready for publishing. I want to not have to worry about money. I want to not constantly being thinking these negative thoughts. I want to be loved. I want to be fucked.

I want.
